blocks.content: Team: Consultify
Members: Fatima, Kseniia
Repository: https://github.com/ksublo/consultation_reservation_system
The repository is currently private.

items: Domain: university teacher consultation slot reservations.
Resource: a specific consultation slot.
Reservation: student, selected slot, title and description of the reason, and status.
User: a student creates a reservation; a teacher creates slots and approves or cancels reservations.
States: PENDING, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED.
Operations: create a slot and reservation, approve, cancel, and check availability.
Common rule: two active reservations cannot exist for the same slot; both PENDING and CONFIRMED block the slot.
Domain rule: a slot can only be created on weekdays between 07:15 and 19:15. A student can have at most five pending reservations.
System boundary: Notification Service (still in development).
Monorepo with frontend/ and backend/ folders.
Frontend: React, TypeScript and Vite.
Backend: Java 21, Spring Boot and Maven.
Persistence: PostgreSQL and Flyway migrations.
README and documentation in docs/ exist; the repository is ready for shared work.

blocks.content: The complete Project Frame is filled in docs/intent-and-change.md. It describes the system purpose, roles, concepts, persistent state, operations, reservation state transitions, business rules, Notification Service, assumption and an open question.
Category: C — Changeability.
Future change: a teacher will be able to reject a reservation with a reason. A REJECTED state will be added and the slot will become available to other students again.
This is relevant because the change affects the state model, history, business rules and frontend.

Tasks follow the team workflow. One team member implements a change in their own branch, another member reviews it in a pull request, and the change is merged into main after approval. The review verifies functionality, readability, project rules and conflicts.

We verified real reservation persistence in PostgreSQL. Docker Compose runs the database, backend and frontend; Flyway creates the schema and demo data at startup. The backend reads slots through the REST API and data can be verified in the database.

items: Evidence: compose.yaml, DOCKER.md and Flyway migrations in backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/.
Result: availability is protected by both the backend and database constraints, so two active reservations cannot exist for the same slot.

blocks.content: docker compose up --build

Evidence is documented in docs/evidence-and-evolution.md: the question verified PostgreSQL reads and writes; Docker Compose was used for the run; Flyway migrations and visible demo slots were observed. Decision: PostgreSQL, Flyway and Docker Compose remain the standard for local startup and database schema management.
POST /api/reservations → validation → persist to PostgreSQL → 201 Created with reservation ID → automated integration check. The definition is in README.md.

The reservation domain, Resource / Reservation / User model, states, operations, rules, system boundary, Project Frame, selected future pressure, review workflow, engineering spike, evidence and CP1 skeleton are described and evidenced.

The application already supports reservation creation, available slot viewing, teacher approval and reservation cancellation. The overview distinguishes completed implementation from documentation still required for C02.
The following is a proposed baseline based on actual application behaviour. In our process Create makes a PENDING request and a separate Approve changes it to CONFIRMED.
Goal: a student submits a consultation request for one teacher slot.
Trigger: an authenticated student selects a slot, consultation title and description, then submits the form.
Observable requirement: the system creates one PENDING reservation and returns its identifier and state.
Preconditions: student and slot exist; the slot is ACTIVE and future; the student has fewer than five pending reservations and has no overlap with another active reservation.
Success state: the new PENDING reservation blocks the slot and creation is written to reservation_history.

items: Success: submit → validate slot and rules → persist PENDING → return 201 Created.
Failures: unknown student/slot, inactive or past slot, blocked slot, student overlap or exceeded limit → no reservation is created.

blocks.content: Still required: team acceptance as REQ-01 and automated successful and negative verification.
Goal: a student or teacher can identify usable consultation slots.
Observable requirement: the system returns only future ACTIVE slots without a PENDING or CONFIRMED reservation.
Success state: a slot list is returned; no reservation or slot is changed.

items: Success: load active slots → exclude past and blocked slots → return available slots.
Boundary: a past, cancelled or PENDING/CONFIRMED occupied slot is unavailable.

blocks.content: Still required: explicit acceptance of [start, end) interval semantics and verification examples for adjacent and overlapping intervals.
Goal: a teacher accepts a pending request as a confirmed consultation.
Observable requirement: only the owner of the slot can change PENDING to CONFIRMED.
Preconditions: the reservation exists, is PENDING and the actor owns the slot.
Success state: status becomes CONFIRMED and history is stored.

items: Success: teacher confirms → ownership and state are validated → status becomes CONFIRMED.
Failures: other teacher/student → 403; CONFIRMED/CANCELLED source state → rejected without change.

blocks.content: Still required: a complete standalone Approve specification for v0.2 and a concurrency-conflict test.
Goal: a student or teacher cancels an active future consultation and releases its slot.
Observable requirement: a PENDING or CONFIRMED reservation can become CANCELLED at least three hours before its start.
Success state: actor, note, cancellation time and history are stored; the slot stops being blocked.

items: Success: authorised actor cancels → backend validates state, ownership and time → persists CANCELLED.
Failures: unrelated actor, already cancelled reservation or less than three hours before start → no change.

blocks.content: Still required: team rationale for the three-hour limit and automated boundary tests at exactly three hours.
Meaning, need, observable result, feasibility, verifiability, state/time, concurrency, consistency and uncertainty must be reviewed by the team for every accepted requirement.
Still required: record this review for REQ-01 to REQ-04 and mark Baseline v0.1 as team-approved.

items: BR-01 Intervals: slots use [start, end) semantics; one slot may end exactly when the next begins.
BR-02 Exclusivity: one slot cannot have more than one active PENDING or CONFIRMED reservation.
BR-03 Cancellation: an authorised actor can cancel an active reservation at least three hours before start.
BR-04 Domain rule: teachers create slots only on weekdays from 07:15 to 19:15; students have a pending-reservation limit and no active overlap.

blocks.content: Still required: formally approve these rules and reference them from OP-01 to OP-04 instead of duplicating their wording.

items: Create Reservation: a student creates a reservation for an active future slot; its resulting state is PENDING.
Check Availability: frontend and API show only active, available slots; PENDING and CONFIRMED block a slot.
Confirm / Approve Reservation: the slot owner can change PENDING to CONFIRMED.
Cancel Reservation: a student or teacher can cancel an active reservation at least 3 hours before its start; the record remains in history.
Rules in code: weekdays 07:15–19:15, pending reservation limit, student overlap control and one active reservation per slot.
The database treats PENDING and CONFIRMED reservations as blocking states and stores change history.

blocks.content: The diagrams below reflect the current PENDING, CONFIRMED and CANCELLED process. Their conditions must be aligned with the final v0.2 text baseline before submission.
A student creates and cancels their own reservations; a teacher checks availability, approves requests and cancels reservations for their slot.
A reservation starts as PENDING, a teacher can confirm it to CONFIRMED, and active reservations can be cancelled to CANCELLED according to the policy.
The diagram covers availability checking, creation, confirmation and cancellation including principal validation decisions.
